title: Magnon-polaron mediated spin Seebeck effect in altermagnets
authors: Ilia Moghayer, Ritesh Das, Yaroslav M. Blanter
abstract: Altermagnets, distinguished by compensated antiparallel spins yet nondegenerate magnon spectra, bridge the gap between ferromagnets and antiferromagnets. Although several probes such as anisotropic transport and spectroscopic measurements have been proposed to identify altermagnetic order, experimentally accessible transport signatures remain highly desirable. Here, we show that in altermagnets subject to an external magnetic field, the spin Seebeck effect exhibits pronounced directional anisotropy. Specifically, the spin Seebeck coefficient differs significantly along in-plane directions, and this anisotropy increases with field strength. Magnetoelastic interactions further produce resonant peaks whose positions with respect to an applied magnetic field reflect the intrinsic magnon band anisotropy, and provide localized features that enhance the distinguishability of the altermagnetic response. The peaks provide a robust experimental signature of altermagnetic order. Our findings serve as signatures of altermagnetic order while laying the groundwork for their application in spintronic devices.
summary: This work proposes using the Spin Seebeck Effect (SSE) as a definitive experimental probe to identify altermagnetic materials. By modeling magnon-phonon coupling, the authors predict that altermagnets will exhibit unique directional anisotropy and field-dependent resonant peaks in the SSE that are absent or different in conventional antiferromagnets.
main_problem: To find experimentally accessible transport signatures that can distinguish altermagnets from conventional ferromagnets or antiferromagnets.
main_result: The Spin Seebeck Effect (SSE) exhibits pronounced directional anisotropy and resonant peaks whose positions depend on the measurement direction in altermagnets, providing a robust diagnostic signature.
method: Theoretical calculation using Boltzmann theory to model spin transport mediated by magnon-phonon hybridization. The analysis compares theoretical predictions for altermagnetic versus antiferromagnetic coupling regimes.
model_or_system: The study uses a minimal lattice Hamiltonian describing collinear magnets with compensated antiparallel spins (altermagnets). It incorporates magnetoelastic interactions leading to hybridized 'magnon-polaron' modes.
key_observables:
Spin Seebeck coefficient ($S_{\alpha eta}$), directional anisotropy of SSE ($S_{xx} 
eq S_{yy}$), and resonant peak positions as a function of applied magnetic field.
important_parameters: External magnetic field strength ($H$), exchange couplings ($J_1, J_2, J'_2$), and phonon coupling strengths ($\Gamma, \kappa$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the spin-wave approximation for magnon dynamics and assumes that magnon-polaron modes are well-defined quasiparticles.
figures_summary:
Figures compare magnon dispersion relations (A vs B modes) between altermagnetic ($J_2 
eq J'_2$) and antiferromagnetic ($J_2 = J'_2$) states, showing directional anisotropy in the SSE response as a function of magnetic field.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical distinction between magnet types using magnon dispersion theory to calculating the measurable transport signature (SSE) by incorporating phonon coupling via the Boltzmann equation.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter magnetism, the use of quasiparticle descriptions (magnon-polarons) and non-equilibrium transport calculations touches upon concepts relevant to open quantum systems dynamics and energy/momentum transfer in correlated media.

FIG. 3: SSE vs. applied magnetic field in-plane along the x and y directions with magnetoelastic coupling for (a) an antiferromagnetic lattice and (b) for an altermagnetic lattice in the monolayer limit. Peaks in SSE are seen at the same magnetic field for the antiferromagnetic case in both S2D xx and S2D yy . For the altermagnetic case, the peak in S2D xx appears at a magnetic field different from the peak in S2D yy . The features are seen clearly by calculating the difference in SSE due to phonons (c) ∆Sxx and (d) ∆Syy vs. magnetic field. τm is the magnon lifetime.
